skill_traces.query:
Andrew: Hey Audrey! How are you? My GF and I just had a great experience volunteering at a pet shelter on Monday - it was so rewarding! We loved spending time with those cute animals and it gave us so much joy. It was so rewarding, it reminded me just how much I love them!
Audrey: Hi Andrew! I'm good, thanks. That's awesome about the pet shelter volunteering. Helping animals really is great and you can tell when they're happy! So happy for you getting to experience that! I should do that someday too!
Andrew: Thanks! Seeing them so content makes me happy, it really makes me realize how special and full of love they are! Have you ever volunteered at an animal shelter? It can be so rewarding. 
Audrey: Never been to an animal shelter before, but it must be great! My four fur babies are more important to me than anything! Here's a pic of us from a fun day out at the park.
Andrew: Aww that's a cute photo! How are their personalities? Tell me more!
Audrey: Well the oldest one is the most relaxed, like a wise old sage. The second one is always ready for a game. The third one can be naughty but loves a good cuddle. And the youngest one is full of life and always up for an adventure. They all have their own individual personalities and I adore them.
Andrew: Wow, they sound amazing! They must remind you of your childhood pup. That photo of you with your dog is so cute, he looks like the most playful one ever! Pets really do bring so much joy in your life!
Audrey: Thanks! That one is Max, my childhood dog. He had lots of energy and loved a game of fetch. I have lots of great memories with him. Pets sure bring a lot of joy.
Andrew: Yeah! Their love and energy can really brighten up a day. It's amazing how close we can get to them and the memories they create for us. Do you have any other special memories with Max that you remember fondly?
Audrey: Max and I would take long walks in the neighborhood when I was a kid. We explored new paths, him sniffing and marking his territory. We grew really close, and I shared my worries and hopes with him. He was a great listener, always there for me. Those days are some of my favorite memories. 
Andrew: Pets are more than just pets - they become friends and confidantes. They always know how to listen and provide comfort when we need it. They can make us feel so loved and understood, leaving a lasting mark on our lives.
Audrey: Pets truly make our lives so much better. They listen without judging and give us the best unconditional love. They always leave a mark in our hearts and remind us how it feels to be seen and understood. I'm thankful to have them around - they bring so much joy, comfort, and love.
Andrew: You nailed it! That's why we went volunteering with animals. It has been one of the most rewarding things I've ever done. They really do lift our spirits with all their love, joy, and comfort.
Audrey: I'm so glad you guys got to experience that! Animals really have a way of brightening our day and giving us lots of love and joy. I'm sure the pet shelter really appreciated your help too!
Andrew: Yeah we had a blast volunteering. It's our way of giving back and making their lives better!
Audrey: I'm sure your kindness and care will make them happier no doubt!

selected.name: Extract Comfort and Joy Sources
selected.description: Use when a message states that something cheers the user up, brings joy, or provides comfort.
content: During extraction, if the user mentions a pet, hobby, person, item, or activity that provides cheer, comfort, or emotional support, create a separate durable memory (preference, relationship, or state) capturing that source, even when the message also contains stress or negative events.
Do not merge the supportive source only into a negative-event candidate; it should be its own candidate so it survives later SKIP/MERGE decisions.
Extract only sources explicitly stated as supportive; do not infer unmentioned ones.
selected.rerank_reason: The conversation repeatedly mentions how pets bring joy, comfort, and emotional support, which directly aligns with the skill's focus on extracting sources of comfort and joy.

selected.name: Extract Explicit Relational Framing
selected.description: When a user explicitly states how they view a person, pet, or group (e.g., 'pets are family', 'feel like family'), during extraction.
content: During extraction, if a user explicitly declares how they view someone or something (e.g., 'pets are family', 'my little family', 'feel like family', 'as a friend'), create a separate profile or relationship memory capturing that view, even if the message also contains event details like photos or activities.
Use memory kind 'relationship' when the statement defines a connection between the speaker and the subject; otherwise use 'state' or 'preference' for attitudes and values.
Apply to both first mentions and repeated mentions across sessions; record the view as a durable memory rather than folding it into an event memory.
Only extract when the framing is explicit or strongly implied; do not infer relationships from generic pleasantries, compliments, or small talk.
Stop after capturing the explicit view in one memory per stated relationship; do not add redundant memories for every photo or activity that merely implies the same view.
selected.rerank_reason: Audrey explicitly frames her pets as important and loving, indicating a relational view that aligns with the skill's purpose of capturing explicit relational framing.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract Pet Activity Memories
nearby_not_selected.description: When a user mentions doing an activity with their pet (e.g., walking, hiking), during extraction.
content: During extraction, treat any explicit statement where the speaker describes performing an activity with their pet as a candidate memory, even if it appears in casual sign-off or small talk.
Record the activity and the pet name as the object (e.g., 'walks with Buddy', 'hikes with Toby'), with the speaker as the subject.
Resolve relative time from the message timestamp; if the activity is described as a general habit, capture it as a state; if it is a one-off event, capture it as an event.
Stop after capturing the stated activity; do not infer additional pet facts or unrelated activities unless explicitly mentioned.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract Shared Bonding-Activity Memories
nearby_not_selected.description: When a user reflectively describes a past shared activity with a specific person and frames it as bonding, making memories, or quality time.
content: During extraction, treat first-person statements about a past shared activity with a named person that explicitly mention bonding, making memories, closeness, or quality time as a durable event or relationship memory candidate.
Capture the activity, the companion, and the relational framing.
Do not require explicit fact-like phrasing; reflective storytelling is sufficient evidence.
Create at most one candidate per distinct activity-and-companion pair, and skip statements that name no specific person or activity.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract Family Pet Ownership
nearby_not_selected.description: When a speaker references a pet as belonging to their family or household (including via a photo), during extraction.
content: During extraction, if a message links a pet to the speaker's own family or household (e.g., 'my family's dog', 'our dog', a photo described as my family's pet), create a memory that the speaker had that pet.
Do not require an explicit statement like 'I grew up with a dog'; owning a family pet in the past implies it was part of the speaker's upbringing.
Skip pet mentions that clearly belong to someone else (e.g., a friend's dog) or that are generic with no owner.
Record the speaker as subject and use event or relationship memory kinds as appropriate; stop after extracting the ownership fact—do not expand into extra searches or unrelated pet details.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract Offers, Encouragement, and Advice
nearby_not_selected.description: Use during extraction when a message contains one person offering help, giving advice, encouragement, or reassurance to another person.
content: During extraction, treat a single message as sufficient evidence when a speaker offers help, gives advice, encouragement, or reassurance to another person.
Create one event memory capturing the speaker, the recipient, and the gist of what was said, including any explicit guidance or offer topic.
Stop after the gist is captured; do not infer the recipient's internal feelings or expand into multiple memory kinds unless the message contains other distinct facts.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract user-stated activity frequency
nearby_not_selected.description: When a user explicitly states how often they do a recurring activity, extract a durable memory with the activity and frequency.
content: During extraction, when a user explicitly states the frequency of a recurring activity (including colloquial phrases like 'very often', 'all the time', 'a couple times a week'), create a candidate memory capturing both the activity and the frequency.
Use memory kind 'state' for habitual routines and 'event' for scheduled recurring occurrences; resolve relative time from the message timestamp.
During CRUD, if a matching memory for the same activity already exists, UPDATE or MERGE it rather than adding a duplicate.
